_label: baseline — PROVISIONAL TESTING VALUES. Simulation assumptions, NOT design locks.
name: baseline

compatibility._label: Combo fit. ONE shared grade per EXACT genre+theme pair, applied identically to Audience and Critic scores (PROD-062). Audience/Critic differences come only from craft weights (audienceWeights 35% Filming + 35% Editing vs criticWeights 35% Plot + 35% Writing). mode random = legacy regression only: two independent weighted grades from the world stream (every earlier gate). mode editorial = the designer-editable matrix below, optionally shifted by a bounded per-pair variation from a stable hash of (seed, pair), never a shared RNG stream. The random draws are still consumed in editorial mode so every other world/talent draw is unchanged. Grades are EDITORIAL PROPOSALS for designer review; 'contestable' pairs carry the pick and the reason.

variation._label: bounded world-to-world variation: each pair's single grade shifts one step with this chance (direction 50/50, clamped A..F).

contestable.Action|Dinosaurs: B (draft A/C). Huge crowd concept, but usually dumb fun; B keeps it a strong pick without being a no-brainer A.
contestable.Comedy|Sports: A (draft A/B). Sports comedy is a proven sweet spot (underdog team + slapstick); deserves top fit.
contestable.Comedy|Zombies: B (draft B/B). Zombie comedy works (spoof energy) but is a niche; B, not A.
contestable.Horror|Spies: D (draft D/F). Strange mix, not nonsense; keep F for pairings that fight each other outright.
contestable.Horror|Pirates: C (draft C/D). Cursed-ship / ghost-crew horror is a real subgenre; middling, not bad.
contestable.Thriller|Time Travel: A (draft B/A). Loops, paradoxes and countdowns are thriller fuel; one of the best thriller fits.
contestable.Romance|Zombies: D (draft D/F). Can work as a rare oddball love story; poor, not impossible.
contestable.Romance|Vampires: B (draft B/D). Brooding immortal romance is a big crowd draw; critic snobbery now comes from craft weights, not the grade.
contestable.Romance|Robots: C (draft D/C). Lonely-human/AI love stories land often enough; average fit.
contestable.Drama|Zombies: C (draft D/C). Survival drama with zombies as backdrop is a proven prestige-TV shape; average fit.
contestable.SciFi|Dinosaurs: B (draft B/C). De-extinction / lost-world sci-fi is the genre's natural home for dinosaurs.
contestable.RomCom|Zombies: D (draft D/F). Comedy softens the gore a little; still poor.
contestable.RomCom|Spies: C (draft B/D). Married-spies action romcom is popular but rarely good; split the difference.

compatibility._matrixNote: Collapse rule for the old two-grade draft: crowd genres (Action, Comedy, Horror, Romance, SciFi, RomCom) keep the draft AUDIENCE grade, prestige genres (Drama, Thriller) keep the draft CRITIC grade; contestable pairs use the pick above.

cult._label: Gate 4Q EXPERIMENT, default OFF. Rare audience-only reception exception at release ('Unexpected cult appeal'). Eligible only when: the pair's audience grade is in eligibleAudienceGrades, the studio has never released this exact pair before (novelty), and audience-side craft (mean Filming+Editing quality) >= minAudienceCraft. chance = baseChance + trend bonus; drawn from the lazy 'reception' stream. Success replaces the AUDIENCE grade used in the normal score formula (lift = +liftSteps; breakout = breakoutGrade) for THIS title only; critics, meters, Star, money untouched (money follows the normal audience model). The combo book keeps the true baseline grade.

studioGenre._awardTiming: WORKING ASSUMPTION: genre XP awarded on production completion

scoring._starScoreBonusLabel: PROD-051 option B (designer 2026-11-11), TEST VALUES: a flat Star bonus AFTER the meter curve, sized by skill fit (never Fame): Audience += audience x fit/100, Critic += critic x fit/100. Fit 80 = +0.40 / +0.16 = about +0.3 average, the same all career. The Star's Filming points (production.starFilmingWeight) still apply on top. taperFrom (null = off) fades the bonus to 0 between that score and 10, to protect the 9.0 Hall of Fame line (reports/star-xp/bonus-check.md). Legacy overlay sets 0.

pool._label: Stars rework (PROD-213…218). Persistent talent pool generated ONCE at game creation from the seed (own 'pool' RNG stream, so no other draw moves), a yearly debut class, offscreen careers + retirement, years active (Fame correlates with career length), per-Star hidden growth weights rolled from internal templates, a catalog that unlocks with the first studio upgrade, an 'original lead' card on sequels/new seasons, and a useful free fallback Star. ALL NUMBERS ARE TEST VALUES. legacy-advance.json turns the whole block off (legacy byte-identical).
pool._fameLabel: Fame inside the tier band = lo + (hi - lo) x (fameByYears x yearsPosition + (1 - fameByYears) x random): more years active -> generally more Fame.

offscreen._label: Once a year every non-retired Star not cast in your current production ages one year, may retire, then may rise (Fame up, maybe a level) or fade (Fame down). 'young' = fewer than youngYears years active. Tuned so the big-name tier holds ~30 active Stars over 10 years (reports/stars/summary.md).

growth._label: Per-Star hidden growth weights: a template (internal only, never shown) + per-family jitter, normalised. Level-up points go by these weights; per-film practice still adds growthPerProject to the worked family. levelUpPoints + 2 films x practice = budgetPerLevel, so the budget stays the limit.

catalog._label: Unlocks with the first studio upgrade (staff-capacity ladder). If the config has no ladder, it unlocks at unlockPrestigeWithoutLadder Prestige instead (the first ladder step's Prestige in gate3.json). Flags up to perfectFitTop catalog Stars with family skill >= perfectFitMin as 'perfect for this role'.

fallback._label: Free fallback Star: skill focused on the production's family, about an average paid newcomer (measured in reports/stars).

audience._movieDudLabel: Producers dud fix (PROD-092/208), TEST VALUES: MOVIE-only word-of-mouth pivot (diffusion legs only); null = use qualityPivot. TV/limited series keep the global pivot (PROD-209). Legacy overlay sets null.
audience._qualityPivotLabel: Gate 4 SENSITIVITY knob: score where in-run buzz / word of mouth / episode retention turn from negative to positive (weekly diffusion + episodic models only). 5 = every earlier gate.

diffusion._label: WORKING ASSUMPTION (Gate 2.5 candidate): finite awareness diffusion. Used only when legsModel = 'diffusion' (the Producers default since 2026-11-10; legacy overlay = geometric). movieBadInterestDecay = MOVIE-only override of badInterestDecay (null = global).

prestige._repeatScopeNote: WORKING ASSUMPTION (Open in v9.61): each milestone pays once per IP. Options: perRelease | perIP | career

debug._note: TEST-ONLY regression injection: none | advanceAsRevenue | fameIntoScore. Must be 'none' for real runs.

staffCapacity._label: EXPERIMENTAL (Gate 2.5). Studio-wide max employees; NOT a per-project crew cap. Baseline keeps the historical uncapped behavior for comparison.

agents._label: Agent-only heuristics (not game rules). legacyHeuristicStaffCaps reproduces pre-Gate-2.5 strategy hiring cutoffs (balanced 4, quality-first 5, others never hire). tvOrderPreference (Gate 3): Gate 3 agents order the largest allowed TV season up to this size ("max" or a number). useFiring / economicRenewal (Gate 3 follow-up, Gate 3 policies only): dismiss the weakest employee to make room for the Software Engineer or when cash < fireDebtThreshold; renew a show only while its last finished season netted >= renewMinNetPerWeek per production week (replaces the old fixed policy season limits). Both false = the original Gate 3 policies.

expectations._label: EXPERIMENTAL (Gate 2.6). HARNESS PROXY for critic generations (named critics retiring, replaced by a tougher generation) and gentler audience-era expectations. Deterministic, calendar-based, applied after combo/weakness/fatigue/saturation and before the 0-10 clamp, at release time only (published scores never change). Disabled = previous behavior exactly. All numbers are TEST ASSUMPTIONS.

formats._label: Gate 3. LOCKED direction: movies + limited series first, TV via a studio upgrade (money + Prestige), streaming later. All false = the Gate 2.6 movie-only kernel, byte-identical.

limitedSeries._label: TEST ASSUMPTIONS. Self-contained, NON-renewable series: fixed episode package, weekly airing + short tail.

tv._label: TEST ASSUMPTIONS for renewable TV (one IP, separately produced seasons). LOCKED: renewal by season average (4.0 renewable, 9.0 HoF), episode caps by studio Prestige (not show history), genre locked, twist changes theme, hiatus affects anticipation only, announcement = show-specific fading hype.

viewerFatigue._label: EXPERIMENT (Gate 3 follow-up), default OFF. Returning-viewer / season-opening interest fatigue: multiplies ONLY the returning-audience opening inputs (IP fans + announcement anticipation; optionally the premiere share). Never touches Audience/Critic scores, ratings or sales directly. Separate from review fatigue (tv.fatigue), IP fans and hiatus. Offset by: previous-season quality (qualitySlow), a good twist (goodTwistReset units), and every additive opening input it does not touch (marketing, Star Fame, trends, studio buzz) plus in-run critic buzz / word of mouth. basis: seasons = seasons aired; episodes = episodes aired / episodesPerStep. All numbers TEST ASSUMPTIONS.

contract._label: OPEN designer decision. A = every season is a new pitch (fixed offers). B = continuing partner: same distributor + royalty; per-season advance = baseCost x clamp(baseCover + roiWeight x (lastRoi-1), minCover, maxCover) x trust factor.

streaming._label: TEST ASSUMPTIONS for the studio streaming service (one aggregate subscriber business; no per-title payouts).

staffing._label: Gate 3 follow-up. LOCKED: employees can be fired to free a capacity slot (4/6/8 unchanged; the Software Engineer uses a normal slot). Harness UX ASSUMPTIONS: dismissal only between productions; the engineer cannot be dismissed while building; minStaff and fireCost are OPEN (smallest rule protecting the 'production always progresses' invariant).

breakthrough._label: EXPERIMENT (Gate 3 follow-up), default OFF. Rare seeded creative breakthrough DURING production: one draw from the dedicated 'events' RNG stream when a production first enters each listed stage; on success, bonus meter points = bonusShare x that meter's half-point (meterHalfPointPerWeek x duration x era bar), so the effect saturates on already-strong meters and flows to scores only through the normal meter -> score formula. Never edits a result. At most maxPerProduction per production. All numbers TEST ASSUMPTIONS.

economy._label: DEFAULT = late_distribution (PROD-100, Producers economy). mode legacy_advance = REGRESSION ONLY, every earlier gate byte-identical (distributor advances at the pitch, lifeline, surplus); select it with config/legacy-advance.json / legacyConfig(). mode late_distribution: the studio funds base cost, Star and payroll itself; at 80% 2-3 distributors bid ADVERTISING spend + reach for a revenue share (ad money is spent by the distributor, never studio cash); self-distribution fallback; no lifeline. All numbers TEST ASSUMPTIONS.

lateDistribution._label: Candidate bid formula. appeal = 1 + previewWeight x (preview - previewCenter)/previewSpan + trend + fans + Star Fame + known combo (comboBook only) + last-season delta, clamped. Preview = visible meter quality so far, projected to completion (never final scores or hidden combo grades). adSpend = adBase x format factor x appeal x favored x trust factor x jitter; share = shareBase x (1.15 - 0.15 x appeal) x (1.1 - 0.04 x trust). A distributor only bids when appeal >= its minAppeal.

contracts._label: Gate 4 EXPERIMENT: work-for-hire. Zero cost to accept; the client reimburses the studio's payroll + upkeep each contract week (ledger contract_labor) and pays a fixed visible completion fee (contract_fee). Staff gain XP/stats in the contract's meters. Zero Prestige, no IP, fans, release, HoF or catalog entry. One job at a time (uses the production slot). Fees are TEST ASSUMPTIONS. DEFAULT ON with the Producers economy (PROD-118); legacy-advance.json turns it off.
